title: Unique Yield
statement: Implement `solve(items)`. Yield the first occurrence of each string and return those yields as a list, in order. Later duplicates disappear. The producer may keep a set of seen values. It must not need the full output list in order to decide the next yield.
constraints: items is a list of strings
hints: A set records what you have already yielded.
Yield, or append to the result, only when the item is new.
Do not sort. Order is appearance order.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: A generator can remember seen keys without storing the output.

editorial: A generator can remember seen keys without storing the output. The caller materializes the yields. Sorting first would group duplicates and destroy first-seen order, which is a different function from unique-in-order.
